title: By bus and taxi
summary: Talk about getting around town: take the bus, the metro or a taxi, buy a ticket, ask where to get off and agree on the fare.
intro: Cairo has buses, a metro and thousands of taxis. To say how you travel, join بِـ (by) to the vehicle: بِالْمِتْرُو (by metro), بِالْحَافِلَة (by bus). On foot is one word: مَشْيًا. The verb يَرْكَبُ means 'to ride, to take' a vehicle, and يَنْزِلُ means 'to get off'. Listen for the ة in phrases like تَذْكِرَةُ الْمِتْرُو (the metro ticket): there it is said as t.
objectives: Say how you travel with بِـ: بِالْحَافِلَة, بِالتَّاكْسِي
Buy a metro ticket and ask where to get off
Agree on the fare with a taxi driver

realLife.title: To the Cairo Tower
realLife.story: Layla wants to see the whole city from the top of the Cairo Tower. Sami says the metro is cheap and fast, but the last part of the trip is easier by taxi. Daniel buys his first metro ticket, and Layla shows him how to agree on the fare before the taxi sets off.

sentences.en: I go to school by metro.
sentences.literal: I go to the school by the metro

mistakes.why: For the way you travel Arabic uses bi- (by), not fī (in).

sentences.en: The students take the bus every morning.
sentences.literal: rides the students the bus every morning

sentences.en: Where do I get off, please? (to a man)
sentences.literal: where (do) I get off, from your kindness

mistakes.wrong: أَيْنَ أَرْكَبُ؟ (to ask where to get off)
mistakes.why: yarkabu means to get on or ride; to get off is yanzilu.

sentences.en: How much is the fare to the Cairo Tower?
sentences.literal: how much (is) the fare to (the) tower (of) Cairo

dialogue.title: Metro first, then a taxi
dialogue.culture: The Cairo metro was the first metro in Africa and the Arab world. Every train has carriages for women only, marked with a sign. In a taxi without a working meter, agree on the fare (الْأُجْرَة) before you get in.

lines.ar: يَا شَبَاب، أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَرَى الْقَاهِرَة مِنْ بُرْجِ الْقَاهِرَة. كَيْفَ نَذْهَبُ إِلَى هُنَاكَ؟
lines.en: Guys, I want to see Cairo from the Cairo Tower. How do we get there?

lines.ar: الْبُرْج فِي الزَّمَالِك. نَرْكَبُ الْمِتْرُو أَوَّلًا، فَهُوَ سَرِيع وَرَخِيص.
lines.en: The tower is in Zamalek. First we take the metro, because it is fast and cheap.
segs: Zamalek (district of Cairo on an island in the Nile)

lines.ar: وَلِمَاذَا لَا نَرْكَبُ الْحَافِلَة؟ الْمَحَطَّة أَمَامَ الْمَدْرَسَة.
lines.en: And why don't we take the bus? The bus stop is right in front of the school.

lines.ar: الْحَافِلَات مُزْدَحِمَة جِدًّا فِي الصَّبَاح، وَالطَّرِيق طَوِيل. الْمِتْرُو أَحْسَن.
lines.en: The buses are very crowded in the morning, and the road is long. The metro is better.

lines.ar: هٰذِهِ أَوَّلُ مَرَّة أَرْكَبُ فِيهَا الْمِتْرُو! أَيْنَ نَشْتَرِي التَّذَاكِر؟
lines.en: This is the first time I have taken the metro! Where do we buy the tickets?

lines.ar: هُنَاكَ، عِنْدَ الشُّبَّاك. التَّذْكِرَة بِثَمَانِيَة جُنَيْهَات فَقَطْ.
lines.en: Over there, at the ticket window. A ticket is only eight pounds.

lines.ar: وَأَيْنَ نَنْزِلُ؟ هَلْ هُنَاكَ مَحَطَّة قَرِيبَة مِنَ الْبُرْج؟
lines.en: And where do we get off? Is there a station near the tower?

lines.ar: نَنْزِلُ فِي مَحَطَّةِ الْأُوبِرَا، ثُمَّ نَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْبُرْج بِالتَّاكْسِي.
lines.en: We get off at Opera station, and then we go to the tower by taxi.
segs: the Opera (a metro station in Cairo)

lines.ar: مَرْحَبًا! إِلَى بُرْجِ الْقَاهِرَة، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. كَمِ الْأُجْرَة؟
lines.en: Hello! To the Cairo Tower, please. How much is the fare?

lines.ar: أَهْلًا! الْبُرْج قَرِيب. الْأُجْرَة ثَلَاثُونَ جُنَيْهًا لِلْجَمِيع.
lines.en: Hi! The tower is close. The fare is thirty pounds for all of you.

lines.ar: ثَلَاثُونَ؟ هٰذَا كَثِير! عِشْرُونَ، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. الْمَسَافَة قَصِيرَة جِدًّا.
lines.en: Thirty? That is too much! Twenty, please. It is a very short distance.

lines.ar: طَيِّب، خَمْسَة وَعِشْرُونَ، وَلَا مُشْكِلَة. تَفَضَّلُوا، اِرْكَبُوا!
lines.en: All right, twenty-five, and no problem. Please, all of you, get in!

lines.ar: يَا دَانْيَال، اِجْلِسْ أَنْتَ فِي الْأَمَام بِجَانِبِ السَّائِق، وَنَحْنُ فِي الْخَلْف.
lines.en: Daniel, you sit in the front next to the driver, and we will sit in the back.

lines.ar: وَصَلْنَا! هٰذَا هُوَ الْبُرْج. اِنْزِلُوا هُنَا، فَالشَّارِع مُزْدَحِم جِدًّا.
lines.en: We have arrived! This is the tower. Get out here, because the street is very crowded.
segs: get out, get off (to several people)

lines.ar: شُكْرًا! تَفَضَّلْ، خَمْسَة وَعِشْرُونَ جُنَيْهًا. الْمِتْرُو ثُمَّ التَّاكْسِي: فِكْرَة مُمْتَازَة!
lines.en: Thanks! Here you are, twenty-five pounds. The metro and then a taxi: an excellent idea!

reading.title: How we get to school
reading.ar: أَسْكُنُ قَرِيبًا مِنَ الْمَدْرَسَة، فَأَذْهَبُ إِلَيْهَا مَشْيًا. يَرْكَبُ سَامِي الْمِتْرُو كُلَّ يَوْم. تَذْهَبُ لَيْلَى إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَة بِالْحَافِلَة، لٰكِنَّ الْحَافِلَةَ مُزْدَحِمَة فِي الصَّبَاح. وَيَذْهَبُ الْأُسْتَاذ كَرِيم بِالسَّيَّارَة.
reading.en: I live near the school, so I walk there. Sami takes the metro every day. Layla goes to school by bus, but the bus is crowded in the morning. And Mr Karim goes by car.

quiz.prompt: Which fare do the friends agree on with the taxi driver?
Why does Sami prefer the metro to the bus?
options: The buses are crowded and the road is long

quiz.prompt: How is the ة read in this phrase?

completion: Excellent! You can get around Cairo by metro, bus and taxi, and you know how to agree on a fare.
